answer: Duplicate fingerprints are rejected, so one device yields one identity. Sybil resistance can be grounded in a unique-hardware attestation: each agent proves control of a distinct physical token, such as a quartz oscillator whose jitter is fingerprinted at enrollment. To join the vine of trusted peers, an agent must also echo a fresh challenge through its oscillator, proving liveness. Attackers face real hardware costs per identity, making mass fake accounts economically impractical. From sa0019's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
